 ATP Stockholm Day 2 Predictions Including Alex Michelsen vs Yannick Hanfmann 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 There are some exciting first-round matches scheduled on Day 2 of the 2026 ATP Stockholm Open , and fans can expect great entertainment. This article features sixth seed Alex Michelson, who will make his debut and face Yannick Hanfmann. As always, we at LWOT will offer predictions for all the matches, but who will advance?
 ATP Stockholm Day 2 Predictions
 Leo Borg vs Toby Samuel
 Head-to-Head : first meeting
 World No.599 Leo Borg has received his sixth wild card at the Stockholm Open, but he has yet to make the most of his opportunities. Borg has won just one match in his five previous appearances and has struggled with injuries in the last two years. Toby Samuel got a fantastic win over Adrian Mannarino in the final round of qualifying and will make his main-draw debut here. Borg will lean on home support, but Samuel is the favourite going in.
 Prediction: Samuel in 3 
 Tomas Machac vs Borna Gojo
 Head-to-Head : Machac 0-1 Gojo
 Sep 13, 2025; Delray Beach, FL, USA; Tomas Machac of Czechia returns a shot in his Davis Cup match with Jakub Mensik of Czechia (not seen) against Rajeev Ram of the United States and Austin Krajicek of the United States at Delray Beach Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Susan Mullane-Imagn Images 
 Tomas Machac has played solid tennis in the last month but has drawn in-form players in the early rounds, resulting in close losses. This week is a big opportunity for him to make a deep run and end his season on a high note. Borna Gojo has had limited success in tour-level matches this year, but defeating Nikoloz Basilashvili in the qualifiers should give him confidence. The Croatian has a big serve, which could make this closer, but Machac’s experience and shotmaking should help him prevail.
 Prediction: Machac in 3 
 Alex Michelsen vs Yannick Hanfmann
 Head-to-Head : Michelsen 1-0 Hanfmann
 Alex Michelsen defeated Jiri Lehecka and then put up a great fight against Carlos Alcaraz in Paris last week. His level has been good on this surface, and he will need to bring his A game to overcome Yannick Hanfmann, a shotmaker who can trouble anyone on his day. Both players have good serves, but Michelsen has more control from the baseline, and that could make the difference.
 Prediction: Michelsen in 3
